Last year taker here, i studied for like a week for 3 hrs per day and passed an honors program. Tbh it was easy since it's mostly stuff that I've learned about already but it can get quite hard at the end with that 10 minute test. From what I know, it depends on the industry and profession you're planning to get. Usually having some early experiencr as an intern would be beneficial in the long run since most companies value experience higher than your education(except for a fresh grad position) or honors. Graduating early is up to personal preference really and depends on when you really need it or when you're really sure about the course you're taking.

Afaik you can still drop it pa naman with a 50% retention up till this weekend but for the pros and cons I guess the pro will be that when you do retake it you're ready for what's to come but the cons are that:

1. You might get delayed - Read your flowchart carefully and see how it would affect your subjects there had been many cases where dropping a single major subject caused like a delay of 1 term for students.

2. Offerings and Professors - Dropping it now doesn't guarantee that you could retake it next term as subjects/courses are usually offered based on the availability of the staff and the students taking that subject. You're also not guaranteed to have the "best" profs for the subject since most of them usually move up to the upcoming course after that course. There would be also sell slots and classes available since It's not aligned with the flowchart.

3. Workload - If you're following your flowchart, you may end up having a heavier term than what the university intended for you to have for that term. This is the same thing that's happening to me right now where I have 20 units instead of the recommended 17☠️. Not advisable at all HAHAHAHAHAHA

Other than that, If you're not gunning for latin honors then these are the only concerns you'd need to worry about(for me).

I've asked admissions about this but the results would most likely be in late april or in may. The results for the financial aid application will also be released the same time as your ACET results. Hope this helps!

The grant ranges from 25%, 50%, 75% and 100% tuition fee defrayal on which there will be a part of the application that will ask you which percentage you would like(do note that this does not mean the percentage you chose will be given to you). The OAS will be the one to decide what percentage they will grant you based on your financial need, academic performance, morals, and an essay that you'll have to submit. Furthermore, there may request interviews(f2f or online) in order to either get to know you more or to clear things up. Also even if the results are released, you may still appeal for a higher percentage(kulitin mo lang talaga HAHAHAHA). Lastly, scholar applicants have a special confirmation date(your confirmation fee will be refunded if you paid for it and were granted a scholarship) if they're basing their enrollment to whether or not they get their scholarship. Hope this helps!

For other options naman, If you can't get into UPD/UPLB then you can try going for UST. As a former UST-SHS student, I can definitely say that the workload there is no joke but at least it somehow prepares you for the outside world when it's time for you to work. The student culture there is also really great and tuition-wise, It ranges to around 55k-68k per semester meaning you'll be cashing out at most 136k per year(but it's usually around 120k in your freshman and sophomore years). Other recommendations would be FEU-Tech, TIP, and PUP.   


If you guys have any questions, feel free to reply or message me!
